That the defendant No. 19 (Government) contested the suit stating, inter alia, that the suit properties are Government khas land and though the properties were leased in favour of the plaintiffs but at the instance of the defendants the settlement Appeal No. 154 of 1981-82 was filed and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong cancelled the proposals on the basis of materials on record and settlement revision No. 73 of 1984 filed before Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong was also rejected on hearing the parties. There being provisions of appeals before the higher forums, the plaintiffs did not exhaust the same. The plaintiffs have no right, title or possession in the suit land. The suit is barred under section 76(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The property stands recorded in Khas Khatian of the Government. The suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 8. The High Court Division as it appears from the impugned judgment has considered the said G.O. dated 2nd April 1982 and held that neither G.O. nor the implementation clause had anything to show that the same could supersede the provision of section 81B of the said Act which must be complied with in leasing out agricultural khas land and in that respect section 76(2) of the said Act impliedly provided that Government is the highest authority to pass any order as to the settlement and Civil Court could not interefere with the same unless the same is malafide and coram non judice. Admittedly, no lease deed was executed so as to confer any legal right in the plaintiffs. Memorandum issued by the Government and the Rules relating to the settlement incorporated in the Government Estate Manual have no statutory force but merely provide guidelines and cannot be invoked for claiming a legal right. Similarly, the Court would be far exceeding its function if it were to assume jurisdiction to enforce performance of statutory duties by the public functionaries unless person who comes before the Court has an enforceable legal right. Thus one could only avail of the forum of the Civil Court for enforcement of any legal right or to redress the violation thereof.
